children: Corrected assays for SH26-27 at Silver Hill returned 103 g/t AgEq over 17.28 metres, including 416 g/t over 3.60 metres and 1,192 g/t over 0.67 metres. All other reported assay results remain unchanged; additional data is required to estimate true widths.
Corrected grades are substantially higher than previously reported, improving the disclosed intercept's apparent significance.
The higher-grade interval adds evidence of concentrated mineralization within the broader intercept.
A very high-grade internal interval may guide follow-up exploration, but its narrow width limits standalone interpretation.
Mineralization remains open to the south
The result identifies scope for stepout drilling beyond the current interpreted footprint; continuity is unconfirmed.
True widths have not been estimated
Reported widths are core lengths, so true thickness and economic significance remain uncertain.

This is an early-stage exploration result at Silver Hill, with the release stating that the results are preliminary and insufficient to define a mineral resource. Further drilling and pending assays, including SH26-45, would need to confirm continuity and extent for the discovery to become a larger catalyst.
